description:
This remote backcountry hiking trail leads visitors to the headwaters of Flyshacker Creek on the north side of Hell Raving Peak.

Before you visit this area, you should know that this trail is not maintained, and strong route finding and backcountry navigation skills and experience are essential. Please note that there are no facilities at this trail. This trail is restricted to non-motorized use only; motorized vehicles are not permitted on this trail.

This area is home to both grizzly and black bears - be sure to follow bear aware and bear avoidance strategies. Consider doing this trail as a group of at least 3 people, and never attempt to hike this trail alone.

There are opportunities for self-contained backcountry camping at the glacier-fed subalpine lake that marks the end of trail / route. From here, further off-trail exploration of the subalpine meadows and glaciated ridges is also possible.

The views of the glacier on the north side of Hell Raving Peak are absolutely fabulous on a clear day. Hell Raving Peak has an elevation of approximately 2798 m / 9179 ft.

This trail is part of a longer route that actually originates much further north than what is indicated on our current trail maps. When the Halfway South FSR was built a number of years ago, it provided a much shorter and more direct route to reach the north side of Hell Raving Peak, and therefore the first 11 km of the original trail is no longer necessary. It is not known if this portion of the trail is still identifiable or passable.
directions:
Trail head Lat 51.816505?N , Long -124.922572?W

From Williams Lake, travel west on Hwy 20 for about 222 km to the community of Tatla Lake. Continue west of Tatla Lake along Hwy 20 for another 7.5 km and turn left onto the Halfway South FSR. Follow the Halfway South FSR to approximately 16.5 km and keep left at the junction to remain on the Halfway South FSR. Continue to approximately 24.1 km on the Halfway South FSR and turn left. Follow this road for approximately 3.4 km to the point where the Glacier Valley Trail crosses the road. Watch for multiple trees blazed that mark the trail on both sides of the road. Follow the Glacier Valley Trail south and then southwest to the northern flanks of Hell Raving Mountain and the headwaters of Flyshacker Creek.
